intro: Perform accurate pressure bar to psi conversion for European vehicle tire placards, espresso machines, scuba cylinders, and industrial hydraulic systems. Defined as exactly 100,000 pascals (100 kPa), 1 bar equals 14.5037738 pounds per square inch (psi), just below standard sea-level atmospheric pressure (1.01325 bar). Multiply bar by 14.5037738 above, or look up common pressures from 0.5 bar to 2,500 bar below.
alsoWrittenAs: bar to lbf/in², bars to pounds per square inch, bar into psi, pressure bar to psi

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (bar g / psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (bar a / psia)
items: Tire gauges, air compressors, and hydraulic manifolds measure Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~1.01325 bar or 14.696 psi at sea level), so 0 bar g equals 0 psig.
For vacuum chambers or thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) using absolute pressure, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: What is bar in tire pressure?
faqs.answer: Bar is a metric unit of pressure equal to 100 kPa (about 14.50377 psi), widely used on European and UK car tire placards. Most passenger car tires are inflated to between 2.2 and 2.5 bar, which equals roughly 32 to 36 psi.

faqs.question: How many psi are in 1 bar?
faqs.answer: 1 bar equals 14.5037738 psi (commonly rounded to 14.5038 psi). Conversely, 1 psi equals 0.068948 bar.

faqs.question: How do I convert bar to psi?
faqs.answer: Multiply the pressure in bar by 14.5037738 (psi = bar × 14.5037738). For example, 50 bar × 14.5037738 = 725.18869 psi.

faqs.question: What is 10 bar in psi?
faqs.answer: 10 bar equals 145.03774 psi (about 145 psi), a standard pressure rating for water valves and 100-meter water-resistant watches.
